reel · prototype
A 3-minute test

Job applications ask for the same seven things. Every. Single. Time.

Name, email, portfolio link, "why us?", resume, headshot, phone. Reel is a phone app that keeps everything you reuse one gesture away — inside whatever app you're filling. This page fakes two job applications so you can feel it.

The dialA control docked to the screen edge — the Android experience. One-finger gestures, clicks you can feel. The keyboardYour stuff inside the keyboard — the iPhone experience. Search and tap.

Before you start

The vault comes preloaded as Alex Rivera, a demo applicant. Anything you add stays in this browser only — nothing uploads, nothing leaves your device.

The real product inserts into other apps — Safari forms, Gmail, LinkedIn. A webpage can't reach outside itself, so judge the speed and the feel here, not the reach.

Test 1 · the dial

Apply to Northbeam using only the dial →

The round button on the screen edge is Reel. It floats over whatever you're doing — fill the form below without ever leaving it.

No overlays on iOS — the dial is Android's. On iPad the vault rides the keyboard, the share sheet, and the Files app instead.

The moves

Tap the round buttonOpens and stays. Copied something just before? The dial catches it — or offers to, depending on the catch switch below. Spin the ring: it steps one item at a time and settles; the item at the red mark is up. Tap it — copied, receipt, and the dial slips away. One paste finishes the job.
One ring, everything on itYour two pinned items hold the edge slots — same place forever, tap to use — and everything else follows, newest first, all types together. Colour says the type: amber is text, rust is a link, violet is an image.
Hold · slide out · releaseOne finger, never lifting. Hold the button and slide out onto the ring, then arc your finger to spin it. Release on an item to take it and put the dial away.
Hold · drag acrossDrag the button past the middle of the screen and let go — it docks to the other edge and stays there.
Double-tap the buttonYour most recent item, instantly. No dial.
Slow-cycleHold a finger on any off-center item and the ring cycles slowly until you let go.

Three switches below — Catch style, Egress and Preview — change how it feels. Flip one, run the errand again. Copy something in another app pretends you copied elsewhere; Replay first run shows the one-time permission moment.

Preview is the new one: what's up shows at the top of the screen, so your eyes can stay up there while your thumb spins down here.

＋ Make it yours

Add your own resume or a photo — a photo joins the dial, a document shows up when you attach above. The file never uploads; only its name is remembered, in your browser.

Also: select any text on this page and a Save to Reel chip appears — write one line of your own cover letter, select it, save it, reuse it on the keyboard page.

Test 2 · the keyboard

Second application of the day — keyboard style

Concept exhibit — the iOS keyboard. This page is the iOS surface: on iPhone and iPad, the vault rides the keyboard. On Android the dial carries retrieval instead — the Android IME is what was cut (2026-08-05). Not being built as an Android keyboard.

Tap into any box and the vault keyboard rises — vault first, keys one swipe left. Three things to try: the search field (it uses our own keys — a keyboard can't summon a keyboard), the Interview thanks card (it asks you to fill a blank before inserting), and the ⇄ done key that hands you straight back to your own keyboard.
